paper_title: Helioscope Bounds on Hidden Sector Photons
coupling_convention: kinetic mixing parameter chi, dimensionless (plot shows Log10 chi; values emitted as 10^(Log10 chi))
notes: Redondo 2008 (arXiv:0801.1527): derives new bounds on hidden-photon kinetic mixing chi from (1) solar energy-loss argument (luminosity in hidden photons < L_sun, including resonant production reaching chi ~ 1e-14 for m ~ 295 eV) and (2) reinterpretation of CAST 2007 axion helioscope data, strongest for 0.01-1 eV. No numerical table is provided; data_points are the combined best-limit envelope reconstructed from analytic formulas in the text (e.g. W = 8e43 chi^2 (m/eV)^4 W, CAST flux limit 1e-5 /cm2/s/keV with F1 fit) and the qualitative description of Fig. 6 (slopes, resonance dip at ~295 eV, validity range 3 meV - 40 keV). Values above ~300 eV are figure-read estimates and are approximate to within a factor of a few. Not a dark-matter search: no local DM density assumed. The 'Gas' filled-magnet curve is a projection and is not included. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.8, 44)) | Vision: Figure 6 of the paper (page 15 image). Traced the 'Helioscope (CAST)' dark-blue curve, which is the paper's main helioscope bound on hidden photons; region above the curve is excluded. Curve has slope -2 below m~0.01 eV, slope -1 up to ~3 eV, steep drop to a trough with minimum chi~1e-12 near m~200 eV, then rises; beyond the dashed vertical line at ~1.5e4 eV (CAST 15 keV energy window) the line is an extrapolation, and the paper notes bounds become indeterminate for m > 40 keV. The T-Lifetime and L-Lifetime curves (solar energy-loss bounds) were not traced; the T-Lifetime bound is actually stronger in the 1-1e4 eV range. No dark matter density assumption (solar-flux bound, not DM).
